mode: Native PostgreSQL built-in B-tree ordering, UTF-8 and standard-compliant strings. External relations and their native collations have the same interpretation on both sides.
structure: A sort key targets either a one-based result position or a closed typed scalar evaluated in the input layout. The input roles are int4, int8, Boolean and text field references, int4 arithmetic, builtin casts and explicitly collated text. Direction, effective NULL placement and key precedence are explicit.
conditions: Output positions belong to the projection. Every input reference belongs to the exact source occurrence and type, including nested expressions. All source keys share the SELECT expression bounds and parameter signature. Native DISTINCT only uses projected positions. A resolved input column appearing in the DISTINCT output can be normalized to that exact position. An unqualified simple output name keeps its normal precedence. A name inside an expression binds to the input.
meaning: Evaluate each key under its native type and collation and compare keys in precedence order with the recorded direction and NULL placement. Apply LIMIT and OFFSET to that row order. Keep results with equal tuples and all result-column names and types. Equal keys do not order rows relative to one another.
sql: Qualify every input field with its generated occurrence alias and emit checked expressions, including parenthesized arithmetic and exact types or collations. Emit a position directly. Write explicit NULL placement. Source keys never add a result column.
observations: Exact key type, input occurrence, storage kind, bound coordinate and direction
Ordered tuples with NULLs and duplicates
Raw source SELECT agreement on result metadata and selected order or native error
Distinct qualified projected key normalized to its owned position
No source ordering dependency on output aliases within an expression

finite.completeness: Recover source shape, typed key and effective direction from the constructed graph. Recover option tokens independently from each recorded analyzed request. Compare every analyzed cell and each directly constructed counterpart. Projection includes a unique tie-breaker where the fixture could otherwise yield distinct but equally ordered tuples.

evidence.P02: The SELECT boundary establishes reference scope, native kind, DISTINCT placement, bounds and signature.
evidence.P03: The order contains only typed operands, positions and native ordering options.

evidence.P05: Final immutable scalar roles and copying of the sort list protect the complete graph.

evidence.Q01: Reject wrong occurrences, wrong kinds and inappropriate DISTINCT placement at the owning boundary.
evidence.Q02: Exhaust the independently recovered syntax and structure grid and explore larger source keys.
evidence.Q03: Reuse the checked expression scope with the same projection and external reference bindings.
evidence.Q04: Compare against native raw and rendered SQL and an independent ordered relation model.
evidence.Q05: Link source allocation, validated constructors, traversal and renderer to the installed distribution.
